Citations in table notes

Source: R/citations.R
apa7_write_bib.Rd

Some table notes cite the articles that describe a method (e.g., the trim-and-fill method in apa_publication_bias()). The references are in a BibTeX file that comes with apa7, and apa7_write_bib() copies it to a document's folder so that the citations in notes can be resolved and added to the reference list.

Usage

apa7_write_bib(file = "apa7.bib", overwrite = TRUE)

apa7_bib()

Arguments

file

path of the BibTeX file to write

overwrite

if TRUE (default), an existing file is replaced

Value

apa7_write_bib() returns file, invisibly. apa7_bib() returns the path of the BibTeX file that comes with apa7.

Details

Citations in notes take one of two forms:

  • text: "(Duval & Tweedie, 2000)", which the author must add to the reference list by hand.

  • keys: Pandoc citation keys, "[@duvalTrimFillSimple2000]", which Pandoc's citeproc (and apaquarto) turns into formatted citations and reference-list entries, if the document's bibliography has the entries.

The form is set by the citations argument of apa_note(), or for all notes by apa7_defaults(citations = ) (or options(apa7.citations = )): "auto" (default), "keys", or "text". With "auto", a citation is written as a key when a Quarto or R Markdown document is being rendered and its bibliography (in the YAML header) has an entry with that key, and as text otherwise (e.g., in the console, or in a table saved with flextable::save_as_docx()). So listing the file written by apa7_write_bib() in the YAML header is enough:

---
bibliography: [references.bib, apa7.bib]
---

with apa7::apa7_write_bib() in the setup chunk. The citation keys are those that the Better BibTeX extension for Zotero makes by default (e.g., eggerBiasMetaanalysisDetected1997), so entries exported from Zotero with the same keys work, too.

Citations in notes from apa_flextable(note = TRUE) and the apa-note chunk option of apaquarto are resolved when the document is rendered. Citeproc does not see text that skips Pandoc (e.g., a flextable saved directly to a Word file), so "auto" writes text there.

Examples

# In a document's setup chunk: apa7_write_bib("apa7.bib")
path <- apa7_write_bib(tempfile(fileext = ".bib"))
readLines(path, n = 8)
#> [1] "% References cited in apa7 table notes."                                               
#> [2] "% Exported from the apa7 collection in Zotero (Better BibTeX citation keys)."          
#> [3] "% Write a copy to a document's folder with apa7::apa7_write_bib()."                    
#> [4] ""                                                                                      
#> [5] "@article{beggOperatingCharacteristicsRank1994,"                                        
#> [6] "  title = {Operating Characteristics of a Rank Correlation Test for Publication Bias},"
#> [7] "  author = {Begg, Colin B. and Mazumdar, Madhuchhanda},"                               
#> [8] "  year = 1994,"
